notice: LOCAL RESEARCH ATTESTATION (native-assisted gate). Not an IEANTN verification receipt, not issued by Comparator, not an official justification. Native evaluation extends the trusted base; restricted-C/RN64 semantics, compiler, runtime and hardware are trusted.
promotion_rule: No local attestation promotes anything. An endpoint's official kind may become `lean-comparator` only when the IEANTN verification workflow records an authentic Comparator receipt for that same conclusion (receipts/<Node>.<conclusion>.json), which requires a proof whose axiom closure is exactly propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (zero native facts). The evidence method `lean-verified-program` may then be retained as a description of the proof. A receipt-backed official subtype `lean-verified-program` would need an upstream schema/policy change and is not implemented.

trust_boundary: Native evaluation (native_decide): the Lean compiler and runtime evaluate each listed finite fact; the kernel does not re-check it.
Trusted library implementations reached by those evaluations (implemented_by/extern in Lean core, Std, Batteries, Mathlib) are counted per fact.
Restricted C / IEEE binary64 round-to-nearest model: the proof concerns the modelled execution of the token-matched source, not a compiled binary.
Compiler, host runtime, operating system and hardware are trusted; agreement with GCC output bits is a diagnostic only.
Explicit mathematical hypotheses of the endpoint (listed per attestation) are not proved by it.

Lean exact-dyadic interval backend (lean-dyadic-expr): the proof concerns the evaluation of a generated Lean expression by the vendored LeanCert interval evaluator, not a C program; native evaluation of that evaluator trusts the Lean compiler and runtime.
